mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% over a 3-month period indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC for the UNRATE trigger is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a contraction in both manufacturing and construction sectors, triggering a negative S&P 500 forward 20-day return due to reduced economic activity and corporate revenue outlook.
failure_condition: The interaction between INDPRO and HOUST (measured by their product or joint decline) fails to predict negative 20-day returns, with the Rank IC for the interaction term below 0.03 or the joint decline condition occurring without negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 250), the Federal Reserve's restrictive monetary policy reduces corporate profit margins and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 250, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units signals weak consumer demand for housing, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns due to reduced economic activity and corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 1200.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC for the HOUST trigger is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation (PAYEMS) indicates strong economic conditions and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 in any 1-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad weakening in consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and RSAFS (measured by their joint decline) fails to predict negative 20-day returns, with the Rank IC for the interaction term below 0.03 or the joint decline occurring without negative returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns as investors react to weakening economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 105.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO trigger is below 0.03.
